article.title: Jovan Hadži-Vasiljević
article.description: Serbian historian, ethnographer, journalist and writer
article.extract: Jovan Hadži-Vasiljević was a Serbian historian, ethnographer, journalist and writer.

turns.guesser:
I see Serbia, a man, and a newspaper/writing/books theme. He could be a Serbian writer or journalist, perhaps 19th century, since the emojis suggest folk or rural life and music.

Questions:
1. Is he a writer, a poet, or a politician?
2. Is he from the 19th century or earlier?

GUESS: Vuk Stefanović Karadžić

Understood so far: a writer and journalist, not tied to theatre, active around the time of a world war, a teacher, and perhaps nicknamed "Hadži" after a pilgrimage.

Is the "Hadži" a nickname or title of his? Was he a folklorist or ethnographer? Was he a WWI-era war correspondent?

GUESS: Tihomir Đorđević

Understood: a name linked to the Hajji pilgrimage plus a plant or child element, and strongly tied to folk life and writing. Could the name contain something like "Cvet" (flower) or "Mladen"?

GUESS: Hadži Ruvim

The hint reads as Hajji minus a Greek crown (basileus), giving basil, so Vasilije, and "son of" gives Vasiljević.

GUESS: Jovan Hadži-Vasiljević
